title: Build 162
summary: See what needs your attention from any screen, with a badge on Me.

sections.title: What’s new
items: Me shows the number of actions you can take: an installable box update, your own email accounts that need reconnection, and selected chat or jobs brains that need setup or access.
Opening Me keeps the badge until the actions are resolved. Starting an update removes that action; if it fails and can be retried, it returns. An installed update removes it.
Reconnecting or removing an email account, signing in to a brain, or choosing a ready one refreshes the count. A brain used by both chat and jobs counts once.
The badge and Me cards use the same state. Checks run while the app is active, on return and after reconnection. Old replies cannot bring back resolved warnings or data from a previous pairing.
Temporary network failures, usage limits that reset themselves and unused brains do not create actions. Screen-reader labels explain the count in the app’s language.

sections.title: What to test
items: With a box update available, stay in Chat: Me should show a badge. Open Me and return: the badge should remain until you start or complete the update.
Resolve an owned email account’s authentication problem, test it or remove it. Its count should disappear after the box confirms the new state.
Sign in to a selected brain or choose a ready one. Check that the count falls; an unused brain or a temporary usage limit should not add a badge.
Put the app in the background, resolve an action from another device and return. The badge should refresh. Unpair: no box badge should remain in Solo mode.

sections.title: The box
items: This is an app update. No new box release or SD-card image is needed. It uses the settings APIs supported by your box; unsupported features are skipped.
For a new box, start with [image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0), then install box updates from the app.

title: Build 161
summary: Share documents from other apps, manage Shelly gateways and identify temporary files before they expire.

sections.title: What’s new
items: Documents shared from Mail, AirDrop and file previews reach the composer, including temporary files. Import failures show an explanation.
Attachment buttons adapt to screen width and text size, with readable labels.

Home devices are grouped under their gateway. “Find connected devices” is available in the gateway detail, and hides devices already added. Devices that need reconnection remain visible. Currently supports BLU TRV valves paired in Shelly.
Reconnect a Shelly after an address change without losing its name or confirmation settings.

File-expiry messages show the planned deletion date and explain that you have not asked Wollie to keep the file. Open its preview and see the reader’s description when available. Old warnings also gain a file preview.

sections.title: What to test
items: Share a PDF from Mail or an AirDrop preview with Wollie open, in the background and closed. Check that only one attachment is ready before sending.
Increase text size and open the attachment menu: Photo, Camera, Scan and File should stay readable.

In Me → Home devices, check that valves appear under the correct gateway. Open its detail, find connected devices and add one: it should disappear from discovery results. Repeat network discovery: registered devices at their current address should be hidden.
When a temporary-file warning arrives, open its preview, check the description and deadline, then tap Keep it. An already expired file should show a clear explanation.

sections.title: The box
items: Gateway discovery and the new file-expiry messages need box update 0.7.2. Device grouping, document sharing and previews in old warnings are app changes.
For a new box, start with [image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0), then update from the app. Images older than 0.7.0 cannot update from the app.

title: Box update 0.7.3
summary: Wollie can choose the useful text to copy from your request, including a draft email's subject and body, directly where it belongs in the reply.

sections.title: What's new
items: All box brains receive guidance to mark self-contained copy targets according to the user's intent, without a fixed list of field types. Short values use ordinary Markdown code spans; complete drafts use text blocks that keep paragraphs and signature.

An email draft can offer recipient, subject and body separately. Labels, explanations and final comments stay outside the copied text. The same approach works for messages, titles, search queries and other reusable text.

No new API field or database migration is required. Older apps continue to receive readable Markdown replies. This is an instruction to the AI: the targets it chooses depend on the reply it generates.

note: **Use app build 163 or later for inline highlights, copy icons, tappable text and complete draft blocks. The app also recognizes common values in older replies without repeating chips at the bottom. Solo includes the new guidance in app build 163.** This is a signed software update installed from the app. No new SD-card image is needed. For a new box, start with [image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0), then install updates from the app. Images older than 0.7.0 cannot update from the app.

title: Box update 0.7.2
summary: Recover Shelly gateways after an address change, add paired radiator valves, and recognize temporary chat files before they expire. Install this software update from the app without reflashing the SD card.

sections.title: What's new
items: Network discovery recognizes a known Shelly by its hardware address and offers to reconnect it at its new address. Device names and confirmation settings are preserved. Already registered devices at their current address are hidden.

The gateway detail in the app offers **Find connected devices**. Currently, Wollie imports **BLU TRV radiator valves already paired in Shelly**, including multiple valves per gateway. Discovery shows devices still to add or reconnect, and hides registrations that are already complete.

Valves retain their gateway association and can be recovered after a gateway was removed and added again. Both gateway and valve identities are checked; a temperature command checks the valve identity before sending.
Shelly energy meters with BTHome components and a contactor relay, including Pro EM-50, are correctly identified as meters.

Temporary-file warnings explain that the file has not been requested for permanent storage, show a planned deletion date and time, and include an attachment you can open. A single-file reader's description is retained for future warnings when available. Existing files may have no saved description. Warnings respect the longer lifetime of files still protected by a recent analysis session.

note: **Use app build 161 or later for grouped gateway devices, discovery in gateway details, and previews in older file warnings. Older apps keep working. Pair new valves with their gateway in Shelly first, then add them in Wollie. For a new box, start with [image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0), then install this update from the app. Images older than 0.7.0 cannot update from the app.**

title: Build 159
summary: Choose the brain for chat and jobs from the app, control home devices directly, and read scans with your ChatGPT subscription.

sections.title: What's new
items: Me, Brains: sign in with Claude or ChatGPT, or configure an API provider. Choose a brain for chat and scheduled jobs, with sign-in status and supported usage limits.

Me, Home devices: updated readings and switches in the list; tap a device for all readings, manual controls, name and description. Protected devices ask for confirmation when operated from the app too.
Photos, scans, PDFs, Word, OpenDocument and RTF use the selected brain for reading. Fixed scan reading and the creation of summaries for archived documents.
Chat replies keep the final answer without repeating the text shown while Wollie is working. Accented letters are preserved.

sections.title: What to try
items: Me, Brains: check the available brains and the choices for chat and jobs.
Me, Home devices: open a device and check its readings and controls.
Send a scan, ask Wollie to read and keep it, then find it in Documents with the date printed on the paper.

title: Box update 0.7.1
summary: Choose the brain from the Wollie app and control home devices directly. This is a software update for existing boxes, installed from the app without reflashing the SD card or removing household data.

sections.title: What's new
items: Brains from the app: sign in with Claude or ChatGPT, or configure Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi or another compatible API provider. Choose a brain for chat and another for scheduled jobs, or use the same for both. Sign-in status and supported usage limits are shown in the app.

Home devices: live readings and switches in the list, with a detail page for all readings, manual controls, name and description. A device configured to ask before switching also asks when operated from the app.
Photos, scans, PDFs and office documents use the selected brain for reading. Archived document summaries use the brain selected for jobs. Readings stay separate from the chat's context.
Chat replies keep the final answer without repeating the text shown while Wollie is working. Accented letters are preserved.
The box installs the engine versions required by this release after restarting. The first installation can take a few minutes; leave the box powered and connected.

note: **For a new box, start with [image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0), then install this update from the app. Images older than 0.7.0 cannot update from the app. The new brain settings and manual device controls need app build 159 or later; older apps keep working.**

title: Build 156
summary: Calendars and home devices are set up from the app now, several appointments become one confirmation, and you can edit an earlier message and carry on from there. Your box updates from the app too, and there is a new box image to start from, [0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0).

sections.title: What's new
items: Me, Calendars: connect iCloud or another calendar with an app-specific password (the box tries it before saving it), see what is inside, remove it. The box's owner decides whether Wollie asks before writing.
Several appointments at once («add these four exam dates») are one confirmation, with a tick per event: untick the ones you do not want.

Me, Home devices: your Shelly plugs, switches and valves, whether they answer, look for new ones on the network, add, rename, remove. Wollie can put the question back before switching a device, never take it away.

Long press one of your messages: «Edit and continue from here». What came after it disappears and Wollie picks up from the edited message; «Undo» brings everything back. «Reply» quotes a precise message, so Wollie knows what you are answering.
A job that could not run (a usage limit, no internet) leaves a message with «Try again». A photo or file you sent in the chat that is about to be deleted leaves one with «Keep it».
After you confirm something, the chat says «You confirmed» and what, instead of a technical line.
Word, OpenDocument and RTF files are read like PDFs.
Me tab: «Box version», with «Check now»; the box's owner updates it with one tap and sees each step. «Add another device» shows a code and a QR for your iPad or another phone.
A job's result or a reminder shows up in the chat while you look at it. The context line has «compact» on the left and «new conversation» on the right.
With the brain on a compatible endpoint, the jobs that search the web run on Claude when the box also has a Claude key.

sections.title: What to try
items: Me, Calendars: connect a calendar, then ask Wollie to add two appointments at once.
Long press a message of yours, «Edit and continue from here», change it and send; then «Undo».
Long press a reply of Wollie's, «Reply», and ask about that one.

sections.title: The box
items: [Image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0) is the one to flash on a new box: from then on it updates from the app. A box flashed with an earlier image cannot update from the app.

title: Box image 0.7.0
summary: A new box image, and the same version as an update for boxes already on 0.6.1: the box's owner sees it on the Me tab and taps Update now. Wollie is offline for about a minute while the box restarts, and your data stays where it is.

sections.title: What's new
items: Calendars from the app (Me, Calendars): connect iCloud or another CalDAV calendar with an app-specific password, which the box tries before it saves it. The box's owner decides whether Wollie asks before writing.
Several appointments at once are one confirmation with a tick per event; only the ticked ones are written. Times are read on the household's clock, summer or winter time for that date.

Home devices from the app (Me, Home devices): your Shelly devices, whether they answer, a search of the network, add, rename, remove. The question before switching a device is the owner's: Wollie can put it back, never take it away.
Edit an earlier message and carry on from there, with Undo; reply to a specific message.
A job that could not run leaves a message with Try again; a file sent in the chat that is about to be deleted leaves one with Keep it.
Word, OpenDocument and RTF files are read like PDFs.
A box update shows each step as it happens; another device of yours is added with a code and a QR from the app.
Under the hood: the fixes from an adversarial review of all of the above.

note: **Install image 0.7.0 on a new box: from then on it updates from the app. A box on the 0.6.0 image or earlier can't update in place. The new screens need the Wollie app build 156 or later; older apps keep working with this box.**

title: Build 151
summary: The same app as build 150, published again so TestFlight's page shows its new description: Wollie starts on your iPhone, no Raspberry Pi needed. What's new is in [build 150](#ios-150).

title: Box update 0.6.1
summary: The first update for the box that installs from the app: the box's owner sees it on the Me tab and taps Update now. Wollie is offline for about a minute while the box restarts, and your data stays where it is.

sections.title: What's new
items: Several chats: start a new one for each topic, and Wollie names it after your first message.
Scheduled jobs can search the web when their web switch is on, and open pages only on the sites you allow with a tap.
Verified senders: an attachment from a trusted sender downloads by itself only when the sender's own mail provider confirms who sent it. Anything else asks you first.
Box updates from the app: when a new version is ready, the owner installs it with one tap. If the new version doesn't start, the box goes back by itself to how it was before the update.
Under the hood: dependencies pinned with hashes, a sturdier way to ship code to the box, and many fixes from code reviews.

note: **Boxes on the 0.6.0 image or earlier can't install this update in place: they get these changes with the next image. The Update card needs the Wollie app build 152 or later; older apps keep working with this box.**

title: Build 150
summary: Several chats, one per topic: swipe sideways to go from one to the next. And a reading mode for long answers.

sections.title: What's new
items: Chats: tap «New chat» and you are in it straight away; Wollie names it from your first message, and you can rename it any time. An empty new chat you have not written in is reopened instead of making another.

Swipe sideways to go from one chat to the next; the dots under the name say which one you are in, and which one is answering or has a new reply. Rename, reorder and delete chats from the list (tap the name at the top).
Wollie has the same memories in every chat, but each chat only sees its own messages. Reports, notices and Telegram arrive in the main chat.
Reading mode: long-press a message and choose «Reading mode» (or open it from Quick settings). Full screen, an easy typeface, seven sizes, white, sepia or night page.
Scroll back through a chat and a search bar comes up at the bottom: type and press Search.

Scheduled jobs can search the web when their «Search the web» switch is on (on the job's page). Wollie turns it on when a job needs it; with the web on, sending mail, changing the calendar or controlling a device always asks for a tap.
The icons at the top sit on the right, and the cost is no longer there (it is in Settings).
«Tidy above» also takes a number of your own («Another number…»).

sections.title: What to try
items: Tap «Wollie» at the top, tap «New chat» and ask something: the chat gets a name with the answer.
Long-press an answer, choose «Reading mode», then «Aa» to change size and page.
Scroll up in a chat, type a word in the bar at the bottom and press Search.

title: Box image 0.6.0
summary: The box image for Wollie 0.6.0. Flash it with the one-line command on the [site](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/#box), or with Raspberry Pi Imager and `wollie-repo.json`.

sections.title: What's new
items: **Reminders.** Something you have to do, with fixed words, that rings by itself at its time, without asking the AI. Alerts before it's due ("the day before at 17:00", "2 hours before"), repeats, tags, and buttons on the notification to mark it done or snooze it. Today's are on the app's Today tab.

**Portfolio.** Accounts, made of wallets read from their chain or amounts you type for an exchange, with a balance chart in dollars, euros or bitcoin and how it splits. Ten chains now: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Solana, Sui and IoTeX, and a 0x address is read on every one of those that uses it. Each coin has a Market section, and the box re-reads the wallets every hour.

**Signed requests.** At home the app talks to the box over plain HTTP. With app build 147 or later, every request is now signed with a key that stays on the phone, so someone on your Wi-Fi can no longer act as you. It does not hide the traffic: [the privacy page](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/privacy.html#security) says exactly what is and isn't covered.
**Emails you can correct on the confirmation card.** You can change the subject and text before the email goes. The recipients can't be changed there.
**A general off switch** for the box's owner, in the console and in the app. Off means no AI calls and no scheduled jobs; reminders still ring.
**Scheduled jobs** follow any calendar rule, on the household's clock, and a run missed while the box was off is made up.
**The brain** can be Claude or, to experiment, an endpoint of your own that speaks the same API.
The box's Claude command-line tool sends no telemetry, error reports or update checks.

note: **A box you already have:** there is no in-place update yet, and flashing this image starts a box from scratch. If your box is in use, it is fine to leave it on its version for now. Phones on app builds before 147 keep working; once a phone has opened 147, don't go back to an older build, or it will need pairing again.
installation_hint: **New installation:** do not start from an image older than 0.7.0. Use [image 0.7.0](https://simonerom.github.io/Wollie-releases/changelog.html#box-0.7.0), then install updates from the Wollie app. Earlier images cannot update from the app.
